brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 holds pieces (0,0,0), (1,0,0) with a notch at (0,1,0); level 1 holds pieces (0,0,1), (1,0,1) full bases.
bin:0,0,1 and bin:1,0,1 (hex-bin-full-div3, 3 compartments) sit in the level-1 cells.

A drawer-frame notch (notch:0#0,1#notch1, hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) sits at level 0 between the bases. No drawer part was offered (find_sockets family drawer returned none: drawers need the cut face of a half base, and my attempt with a half base beside the full base gave no drawer offer). So the drawer slot is a frame only, with no sliding drawer placed.
capOpenFaces added 14 solid caps on every open face of the four bases; lockJoints added a joint bolt. check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey organizer: level 0 has two full bases and a drawer-frame notch; level 1 has two full bases carrying two 3-compartment bins. All open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. The drawer is not fully delivered: only the drawer frame notch is placed, because no drawer socket was offered on a half base I tried. A real drawer would need a half base with its cut face open, which I did not get working.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
